title: finding(plugin-calendar): the month gridcell speaks its date in the RUNTIME default while the weekday headers beside it honour the resolved locale
body:
Dedupe words: `CalendarView month gridcell hardcoded default locale` · `MonthView aria-label ignores locale prop` · `toLocaleDateString default vs effectiveLocale` · `calendar date label wrong locale` · `plugin-calendar Intl locale inconsistency`

Surfaced by the objectui#10104 dev while routing that file's a11y strings; ⛔ it correctly declined to fold this in — it is `Intl` **argument routing**, ⛔ not a string a pack can reach, so the bounded in-place carve-out's same-defect-class condition fails. ⭐ **Re-read first-hand by the `domain:ui#2` execution seat before filing** (说明 GG). ⛔ No `priority:*` / `type`: the triage seat's sole production. `domain:ui` inherited from the in-flight parent objectui#10104.

## The site, read on `origin/main`

`packages/plugin-calendar/src/CalendarView.tsx:675` — the day gridcell's accessible name:

```jsx
aria-label={`${day.toLocaleDateString("default", { weekday: "long", month: "long", day: "numeric", year: "numeric" })}…`}
```

⭐ **Control in the same command**: `effectiveLocale` — the RESOLVED locale — occurs **8** times in this same file and is what the weekday-header format call is given. ⇒ the resolved locale is in scope at this line and is simply not passed; the zero is a reading, ⛔ not an absent variable.

## The symptom

`MonthView` receives `locale={effectiveLocale}` and honours it for its **column headers**, while each **cell's date** is spoken in the runtime default. ⇒ in one view, a screen-reader user hears the weekday headers in the session's language and every date in whatever locale the machine happens to have.

**Reproduction**: render `CalendarView` with `locale="de-DE"` (or mount under a non-`en` `I18nProvider`) and compare the header text against a gridcell's `aria-label`.

⚠️ The hand-back reports the same `locale`-vs-`effectiveLocale` split at **several other call sites in this file** — ⛔ NOT re-counted by this seat. ⇒ the deliverable is a **sweep with its own criterion**, ⛔ not this one line.

## ⚠️ The site MOVES before this card can be taken

PR **#10142** (objectui#10104) rewrites exactly this `aria-label` — the English frame around the event count becomes a translated one. ⇒ ⭐ **re-read line 675 after #10142 lands**; the `"default"` argument may survive inside the new expression, may have moved, or may already be gone. ⛔ Do not open this card against the pre-#10142 text.

## ⛔ What this card does NOT claim

- ⛔ Not that the packs are involved. ⭐ No key, no translation, no locale file — this is which tag `Intl` is handed, and that is why objectui#10104 could not absorb it.
- ⛔ Not that `"default"` is wrong everywhere. Where a component genuinely has no resolved locale, the runtime default may be the honest answer — ⚠️ and that is exactly the question objectui#10098 records two DECLARED contracts disagreeing about. ⇒ read that card before settling the policy here.
- ⛔ Not that the several other sites are the same defect: unmeasured, named as a sweep rather than a list.

## Acceptance

- Every `Intl` call in `CalendarView.tsx` that has a resolved locale in scope is handed it, under a criterion written down (what counts as 「in scope」, and what a site with genuinely none should pass).
- ⭐ A pin that renders under a non-`en` locale and asserts the gridcell's accessible name is **not** the runtime default's rendering, with a lit control (the weekday header, which already honours the locale, staying correct in the same run).
- The policy for a site with no resolved locale is stated and reconciled with objectui#10098, ⛔ not chosen silently.
